clue.text: Ulysses' wife loses her head about a kind of neckline cover

indicators.note: about means going round, so the trimmed name surrounds the neckline letter
her first letter is dropped, so the name lacks its opening letter

parts.note: Penelope was the faithful wife of Ulysses (Odysseus) in Homer
a V-neck is a style of neckline, giving the single letter

explanation.surface: Penelope, beheaded, wraps herself round some low-cut garment as a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses her head' takes the P off PENELOPE, leaving ENELOPE; 'about' puts that round V.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper sleeve for a letter is a cover, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Visor worn to prevent one from being blinded

definitions.text: Visor worn to prevent one from being blinded

parts.words: Visor worn to prevent one from being blinded
parts.note: a peak or brim worn on the brow to keep glare out of the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: A green celluloid visor worn by card players and editors kept bright light off the eyes.

clue.text: Church member could be my servant

indicators.note: could be suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A parishioner might turn out to be my butler.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a parish vestry, the body running church business, is a church officer.

clue.text: After a breather. 'e makes a thrust

indicators.note: after places the dropped-aitch word behind the organ

parts.note: a lung is the organ we breathe with
'e is a Cockney he with its H dropped, leaving E

explanation.surface: Having got his breath back, he goes for a stab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest, but it is the organ, LUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: To lunge is to make a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing.

clue.text: In a bust-up, soft phrase is possibly the right answer

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: a bust-up is a smash, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: In a row a gentle remark may be the correct thing to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bust-up' rearranges P and PHRASE. The tail 'is ... the right answer' teases: the answer may well be possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and possibly are synonyms, both expressing uncertainty.

clue.text: Tediously familiar — one of William Coke's?

explanation.surface: Something stale and boring, perhaps one of a Norfolk gentleman's possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: William Coke ordered the first bowler hat in 1849, and the bowler was long called a coke; a hat of his would now be an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale and unoriginal; Coke's hats date from the nineteenth century, so one would be an antique piece of headgear.

clue.text: Guild member's a peevish chap

explanation.definitionFit: A freeman of a City of London livery company is a guild member, and liverish means irritable, so a liver-y man is a grumpy one.

clue.text: Lake", as one boy said to another

indicators.note: said marks the words as heard rather than written

parts.note: a boy accepting a dare says you're on

explanation.surface: A lake, named in a dare between two schoolboys.
explanation.walkthrough: One boy challenges another, who replies 'You're on!', and that sounds like the name of one of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Huron is one of the five Great Lakes, between Michigan and Ontario.

clue.text: More orderly than that Latin in a row

indicators.note: in places the Latin word inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
id is the Latin for that or it

explanation.surface: Neater than a line of Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater and better arranged mean the same as more orderly.

clue.text: Sailors' sound increase

indicators.note: sound tells you the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a ship's company of sailors is a crew

explanation.surface: Seamen in good shape grow in number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but it is the homophone signal: A CREW is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest that builds up over time grows, which is to increase.

clue.text: Noise making one see red

indicators.note: the noise is made into something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racket that drives someone into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Eosin is a red dye used to stain tissue on microscope slides: it is the one that makes you see red. Rearranging NOISE gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: This stain colours cells pink-red under the microscope, so it is the agent through which the viewer sees red.

clue.text: Blushing after engineer chap got back

indicators.note: after places the blushing word behind the other two pieces

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow
a blushing face is red

explanation.surface: A man embarrassed after a mechanic's visit regained his composure.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something lost is to get it back, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fabric for cavalry show

parts.note: horse is a collective term for mounted soldiers
Hair is a famous rock musical, a stage show

explanation.surface: Material for a mounted regiment's parade or display.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsehair woven with cotton or linen makes a stiff upholstery cloth, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Colour wash

explanation.definitionFit: A temporary hair dye is called a colour, and to swill something clean in water is to wash it.

clue.text: Point missed perhaps from stupidity

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Failing to see the point might be put down to being slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimness is slowness of mind, a near synonym of foolishness or dullness.

clue.text: One animal with another, tail to head, with a given name

indicators.note: the last letter goes to the front, from tail end to head

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
a mouse is another animal

explanation.surface: Two creatures nose to tail, each bearing a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail to head' moves the final E of PONYMOUSE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A character who gives the work its title, such as the hero of a novel, is named in that title.

clue.text: Measure net for catch

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
a net is a mesh

explanation.surface: Taking the size of a net used for a haul of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle something as in a net is to catch it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Othello follows Carex into battle

indicators.note: follows places the general after the plant

parts.note: Carex is the botanical genus of sedges
Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's general tags after a grass on the way to war.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedgemoor, in Somerset, was the 1685 battle that ended Monmouth's rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedgemoor was the last pitched battle on English soil, an armed engagement.

clue.text: Used as Jeeves was by Wooster

explanation.definitionFit: Being put to work counts as being used, and P. G. Wodehouse's valet Jeeves had a job in the service of Bertie Wooster.

clue.text: — and unbegot" (Housman)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word stands before 'and unbegot' in a line of A. E. Housman

explanation.walkthrough: Housman, in A Shropshire Lad, writes of the time when he was 'unborn and unbegot'; the dash is the word to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet begotten and not yet brought into the world are paired senses of not having come to life.

clue.text: Old Greek's home, or …

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek's dwelling, or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 21 down, but the clue is complete alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the aged, wise king of Pylos in the Iliad, a figure of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Monarch and monk in a state

parts.note: a king is a monarch
Dom is a title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A king and a holy brother in a sorry condition together.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a crowned head is a country, which is a state.

clue.text: … vessels on the beam

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, a vessel

explanation.surface: Ships rolling on a crosswind.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel is a coal barge, as on the Tyne; 'on the beam' looks nautical, but the beam is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelson is a timber laid along the floor of a ship over the keel, a structural beam.

clue.text: An undergarment of French wear

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
de is French for of

explanation.surface: French lingerie put on for wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing, as wear down.

clue.text: Salty lines one associated with New York

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran the railway lines in Britain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Coarse words from someone connected with New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salty lines' looks like crude talk, but BR is British Rail, the old national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The briny is the sea, and briny water is full of salt, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Mountain goat beheads warlock

indicators.note: beheads cuts off the first letter

parts.note: a warlock is a male witch, a wizard

explanation.surface: A wild goat decapitates a sorcerer.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope of high crags.

clue.text: Blue flower waves round secret retreat

indicators.note: round means the waves go about the other piece

parts.note: a swell is a heaving of the sea's waves

indicators.note: retreat means to go backwards, so the secret word is read from its end

parts.note: deep can mean secretive or hidden, as in a deep one

explanation.surface: Breakers crash around a hidden hideaway where blue blooms grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns DEEP into PEED, and 'round' puts SWELL round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, the common blue wildflower of hedges and lawns, is called by this name.

clue.text: Admiral Byrd, say

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan naval commander; Byrd heard as bird, and a male duck is one.

clue.text: A US lagoon might be similar

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form another word

explanation.surface: An American lagoon could resemble another.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are comparable or alike in some respect are similar.

clue.text: This column is personal

parts.note: a newspaper feature where readers air private troubles and lovers send messages, the personal column

explanation.definitionFit: The agony column is the old name for a paper's personal-ads or problem page, so the column is named by this word.

clue.text: Leah's was Laban's and Reuben was Leah's

definitions.text: Leah's was Laban's and Reuben was Leah's

parts.words: Leah's was Laban's and Reuben was Leah's
parts.note: in Genesis Leah was Laban's first daughter and Reuben was the firstborn son of Leah, so the same rank fits both

explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Laban's daughters were Leah and the younger Rachel; Reuben was Jacob's firstborn, by Leah.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Leah among Laban's daughters and Reuben among Leah's sons were firstborn, the oldest child.

clue.text: Beloved proves expensive when in need, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the costly word inside the rearranged letters
perhaps hints that the letters of need come in some other order

parts.note: taken as written
dear means costly

explanation.surface: A loved one turns out to cost a lot when times are hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns NEED into ENED, and 'in' puts DEAR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endeared to people is held in affection, so it is loved.
